lines.trans: Do not cry over Cannes, Fabienne.
The Angouleme festival is very good too.
Are you ready for the departure?
Me, I am staying at the agency.
The boss and Andrea are going to Cannes.
My karma is bad this month.
You are going to be in charge here.

lines.trans: Last year, I had a single phone call.
Someone is really needed to guard the agency.
Holding the fort is very important, Herve.

You will have peace and quiet to work well.
We trust you, my dear Herve.

examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

examples.trans: You're also having lunch with Dany Boon.

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.
examples.trans: There's a macaron on the table.

meanings.note: elle a quarante ans = she is forty

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

meanings.note: as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of
as an interjection: bon, alors... = right, so...

meanings.en: bonne journée = have a nice day

bord.gloss: board, side; maître à bord = in charge

meanings.en: board, edge, shipboard; maître à bord = master on board

examples.text: Vous serez maître à bord ici.
examples.trans: You will be in charge here.

meanings.note: nickname for the press room full of free gifts

examples.trans: Are you going to your desk?

meanings.note: une rue calme = a quiet street
before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.text: J'ai perdu un ami très cher.
examples.trans: I've lost a very dear friend.

meanings.note: before the noun: un ami très cher
after the noun or after être

meanings.note: after the noun: la semaine dernière = last week
before the noun: le dernier jour

pour faire quoi? = to do what?
faire du vélo = to ride a bike, to cycle

falloir.governs: il faut + infinitive, or il faut que + subjunctive

examples.text: Je suis là pour voir Mathias.

examples.text: Je dois voir la pièce cette semaine.

examples.text: Ça ne va pas du tout.

plural tous (pronounced 'tous' with s): merci à tous
